10.7 fix 2026-10-11: TargetResolver.resolve scored candidates without any visibility check, so an off-screen/hidden node that still exposes a strong label (bounds 0x0) could resolve as UNIQUE and be dispatched to. Added an explicit zero-area rejection (bounds.width() > 0 && bounds.height() > 0) matching the a11y dump/tap guards (AgentAccessibilityService lines 199/376/424), so an invisible match now returns NONE. The spec requires invisible/zero-area nodes never be valid tap targets. Regression test zeroAreaTargetIsNotResolved (Phase10AdversarialTest).

3.5 fix 2026-10-11: ObstacleDetector.detect returned Kind.PERMISSION with a grant-selecting dismissLabel ('while using the app'/'allow'/'ok'); isSafeDismiss accepts 'allow'/'continue', so TaskOrchestrator's 9.12 blocker handler tapped the grant control itself for any real runtime permission request (the class comment claimed the caller decides, the code did not). Now Kind.PERMISSION is returned unresolvable with dismissLabel=null, so the orchestrator's existing unresolvable branch stops the run honestly and never dispatches a tap; detection still needs the deny+grant pair so a Settings > Permissions list stays untouched. Regression tests: Phase9UpgradeTest.detectsAndSafelyDismissesCommonBlockers (updated) and OrchestratorLoopTest.permissionDialogIsNotAutoGranted (new).
3.5 invariant recorded in AGENTS.md: a detected runtime permission dialog is UNRESOLVABLE and must never be auto-granted; do not restore a grant-selecting dismissLabel.
